1: Primary request: a mechanical edit applied consistently across many files. Subject: five identical paper document sheets standing in a fanned row; on every sheet the same small amber block sits in the same place and is being swapped for a teal block, with one thin continuous guide line running through the swap point on all five sheets. The feeling: the same careful change, repeated exactly everywhere.
2: Primary request: building something complete from a precise specification. Subject: a long specification sheet on the left made only of rows of checkbox squares, every checkbox ticked; an arrow leads to a compact, neatly assembled machine of interlocking gears on the right that is clearly finished and running. The feeling: every requirement on the list is met by the working mechanism.
3: Primary request: adding a feature to an existing tool while moving its stored data to a new format. Subject: on the left, a simple card board where small colored tag shapes are being attached to the cards; on the right, stacked data boxes travelling on a short conveyor from an old shelf of one shape into a new shelf of a different, more structured shape, nothing dropped on the way. The feeling: a new capability plus a careful data move, done together.
4: Primary request: diagnosing and repairing a fault from a symptom report alone. Subject: a small report card with a warning triangle shape on it; a large magnifying glass hovering over an otherwise orderly grid of identical cells where exactly one cell is subtly out of line; a wrench nearby resting on a tray, ready. The feeling: reading symptoms, finding the one hidden flaw, then fixing it.
5: Primary request: designing and building a small language interpreter from a specification. Subject: a row of abstract token shapes (brackets, circles, triangles, bars — never letters) flowing left to right into a tidy branching tree structure, and the tree feeding into a single glowing result orb on the right. The feeling: raw expressions become structure, structure becomes an answer.
6: Primary request: a storage engine that must stay consistent through crashes. Subject: a sturdy cabinet of labelled-by-color drawers (no text) holding small key and value blocks; a lightning bolt strikes and a power cord lies unplugged beside it, yet every drawer is intact and a narrow ledger tape of small squares runs neatly out of the cabinet's side, recording each change in order. The feeling: power fails, data survives, nothing half-written.
_note: One subject per aim. Public rule: depict the KIND of task (its shape), never task specifics (no function names, clause counts or defect types) — the tasks themselves are unpublished. The shared style block is prompts/style.txt; aims 2-6 also get aim 1's image as a style reference so the series stays consistent.

logo.style:
Use case: logo-brand
Asset type: emblem for a benchmark sub-brand, shown on a dark website header, in a social-link preview card and at 64 px
Style/medium: glossy faceted glass 3D emblem matching a parent mark that is a four-point star made of glass facets — warm amber on the left facets, teal on the right facets, soft inner glow and a soft halo
Composition/framing: one centered emblem, square 1:1, generous margin, reads clearly at 64 px
Color palette: warm amber and teal glass, subtle highlights
Constraints: transparent background; absolutely no text, letters, numbers, digits, logos of other brands or watermarks
Avoid: people, faces, hands, clutter, photorealistic scenes, busy backgrounds
logo.subject: Primary request: the benchmark emblem. Subject: a rising staircase of six glass steps, each taller than the last, the steps shading from amber at the lowest to teal at the highest; resting on the top step is a small four-point glass star of the same faceted style as the parent mark, glowing softly. The feeling: a measured climb, the same family as the parent star.
